base.alt: Concept image: a bright, empty bedroom with dated walls and a bare floor, before any design work.

baseVariants.prompt: A realistic photograph of an EMPTY bedroom in an ordinary 1990s to 2010s Midwest American suburban house, not a loft and not luxury. Bright, open and airy: big windows, lots of soft daylight, light floors. Plain thin builder baseboards, no crown moulding. Eye-level camera standing in a corner. One large, plain, completely clear main wall is fully visible and unobstructed. Nothing hangs on the walls. No people, no plants, no text, no logos. Natural colour, gentle shadows, 4:3 photograph. The walls are painted a dull, dated blue grey that looks a little cold.

editInstruction: Keep EVERYTHING that already exists exactly as it is: the same camera position, lens, framing, walls, wall colour, trim, window, floor, light and furniture. Keep the lighting and exposure identical: do not darken, re-light or add shadows to the walls, floor or ceiling beyond a soft contact shadow directly under the new item. stages.caption: Simple, wide trim, because a quiet room still needs good bones.
A soft wool rug and a low ash bed made up in rumpled linen.
Small nightstands, each with a paper lamp.
A slatted bench at the foot of the bed and sheer curtains that soften the morning.
One ink painting over the bed, and plenty of empty wall around it.
A branch in a clay vase, a couple of books, a plant. That is all it needs.

final.alt: Concept image: the finished Japandi bedroom with a low ash bed in linen bedding, paper lamps, a slatted bench, sheer curtains and one piece of ink art.
